name: REA Group
desc: Operates online property portals including realestate.com.au, earning from agent and developer listing fees, plus financial services and data.
markets: Core market Australia; owns property portals in India through REA India (Housing.com); customers are agents, developers and home buyers.
rationale: Strong Australian consumer brand with Indian growth interests; F1 could support brand reach and hospitality for agents and advertisers, though no obvious tech tie-in.

name: ARKO Corp.
desc: Operates convenience stores and supplies fuel wholesale to dealer sites in the United States under regional banners such as GetGo.
markets: Convenience stores and fuel supply across US regions; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Everyday motorist customers and fuel wholesale make motorsport thematically relevant, but patchwork of regional banners and domestic footprint limit international value.
changed: Formed in 2020 through merger of GPM Investments with SPAC Haymaker Acquisition Corp. II

name: DLF
desc: Develops and sells residential apartments and villas and owns office and retail properties in India.
markets: Home buyers, corporate tenants and retailers in India; no verified overseas operations or expansion plans.
rationale: India's largest listed developer with premium brand, but domestic customers and no international ambitions make F1 a stretch beyond hospitality for high-net-worth buyers.

name: Parkit Enterprise
desc: Canadian listed company that acquires and holds commercial and industrial properties and earns rental income.
markets: Commercial real estate tenants; scope of operations and any international activity not confirmed.
rationale: Small property holder with no consumer brand; little rationale for an F1 partnership.

name: essensys
desc: Provides software platform for flexible workspace operators covering networks, access control, room booking and billing.
markets: Flexible office operators and landlords in the UK, US and Asia, paying subscriptions and usage fees.
rationale: B2B software with customers in several regions; F1 hospitality could suit enterprise sales, but small company with limited marketing budget.

name: LiveTiles
desc: Sells intranet and digital workplace software built on Microsoft platforms, founded in Sydney, to enterprise and government customers.
markets: Enterprise and government customers; Australian origins with New York headquarters; current corporate status not confirmed.
rationale: Mid-sized B2B software vendor could use F1 hospitality for enterprise sales, but current status is unclear and marketing scale is limited.

name: Fronsac Real Estate Investment Trust
desc: Canadian listed real estate company based in Montreal that acquires and holds property for rental income.
markets: Property holdings assumed in Canada; portfolio and scale not confirmed.
rationale: Small Canadian property vehicle with no consumer brand; little commercial case for F1 partnership.

name: The Real Brokerage
desc: Runs cloud-based real estate brokerage in which independent agents earn revenue share, with mortgage, title and rewards products.
markets: Home buying and selling services in the United States and Canada through tens of thousands of agents.
rationale: Agent-recruitment and brand-awareness push in US and Canada; F1 events could offer agent incentives and hospitality, though footprint is North America only.

name: Ardent Communications
desc: Former US broadband provider formerly CAIS Internet that delivered high-speed internet to hotels, apartment buildings and office towers.
markets: Served US properties; went bankrupt in 2001 and no longer operates.
rationale: Defunct since its 2001 bankruptcy and no longer operating, so no F1 partnership is possible.
changed: CAIS Internet renamed Ardent Communications in 2000; bankrupt in 2001

name: Life Storage
desc: Owned and operated self-storage facilities across the United States, renting units to households and small businesses.
markets: Self-storage customers in about 30 US states; no international operations.
rationale: Now part of a larger storage operator with no motorsport tie-in; weak F1 fit.
changed: Acquired by Extra Space Storage in 2023

name: Agung Podomoro Land
desc: Develops integrated townships, apartments, offices, malls and hotels, mainly in Jakarta and other Indonesian cities.
markets: Buyers and tenants in Indonesia; no verified overseas operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Large Indonesian developer with consumer property brand, but domestic customers limit what F1 would add beyond hospitality.

name: Ardstone Homes
desc: Residential property developer building new homes and apartments for the Irish housing market.
markets: Irish home buyers and renters; no verified activity outside Ireland.
rationale: Irish housebuilder with local awareness and no international footprint; limited reason to sponsor F1.

name: Drawbridge Realty Management
desc: Real estate firm based in San Francisco; its assets, clients and current status are not confirmed.
markets: Activities not confirmed; last funding recorded in 2012.
rationale: Unclear what the firm does today or if it still operates; no evident F1 rationale.

name: Nolan Living
desc: Described as a property brokerage in the Kansas City area; its current activities and status are not confirmed.
markets: Kansas City area; last funding recorded in 2012 and current status unclear.
rationale: Unclear whether it still operates and no evident international reach; weak F1 fit.

name: Crombie REIT
desc: Owns about 300 retail, office and mixed-use properties, mainly grocery-anchored shopping centres in Canada, and earns rental income.
markets: Tenants across Atlantic Canada, Quebec and Ontario, anchored by Sobeys; no verified international operations.
rationale: Institutional landlord with no consumer brand and Canadian-only portfolio; little commercial rationale for F1.

name: Clipper Realty
desc: Owns and manages about 10,000 apartments and commercial buildings in Brooklyn, Manhattan and the Bronx, earning residential and commercial rents.
markets: Residential and commercial tenants in New York City only; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: New York landlord without a consumer brand; F1 offers little beyond occasional hospitality value.

name: Paragon REIT (formerly SPH REIT)
desc: Owns Paragon mall and medical suites on Orchard Road, two suburban Singapore malls and an Australian property, earning rent.
industry: retail property real estate investment trust
markets: Retail tenants and shoppers in Singapore with one Australian shopping centre.
rationale: Singapore hosts a Grand Prix and Orchard Road mall draws affluent shoppers, but institutional landlord has little marketing need.
changed: Renamed Paragon REIT after Singapore Press Holdings restructuring, around 2021

name: Invesque
desc: Owns senior housing and care properties in the United States, run through operators, earning rents and resident fees.
markets: Senior housing and care operators in the US; no verified international activity.
rationale: Institutional landlord with no consumer brand and restructuring history; no clear F1 rationale.

name: OUE Lippo Healthcare
desc: Singapore-listed healthcare and property group with clinics and hospitals in Singapore, Malaysia and China plus healthcare property.
markets: Patients in Singapore, Malaysia and China; later renamed OUE Healthcare, current status not confirmed.
rationale: Local healthcare brand with little marketing need; restructured and current status unclear, so weak F1 fit.
changed: Renamed OUE Healthcare

name: Inovalis
desc: Real estate investment manager that buys, manages and renovates office buildings in France, Germany and other European markets for investors.
markets: Institutional and retail investors; office buildings in France, Germany and other European markets.
rationale: B2B asset manager with little public brand profile; F1 hospitality could suit investor entertainment only.

name: Leaders Romans Group
desc: Runs residential lettings and sales branches under the Leaders and Romans brands, plus property investment, land and new homes services.
markets: Local high-street branches concentrated in southern England; no verified international operations.
rationale: Regional estate agency with local brands; British F1 audience is relevant but footprint is too narrow for an F1 deal.

name: HAGL Myanmar
desc: Operates the HAGL Myanmar Centre in Yangon, a mixed-use complex with offices, hotel and retail, earning leasing and hospitality income.
markets: Tenants and hotel guests in Yangon; part of Vietnam's Hoang Anh Gia Lai group; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Single-city property operator with limited recognition outside Myanmar; no clear F1 rationale.

name: Sella Capital Real Estate
desc: Israeli real estate investment company that holds commercial and income-producing properties and earns rental income.
markets: Tenants in Israel, mainly offices and retail space in central Israel; no verified international activity.
rationale: Institutional landlord with no consumer brand and Israeli-only portfolio; little commercial case for F1.

name: Alony-Hetz Properties & Investments
desc: Israeli holding company with interests in Israeli commercial property, North American multifamily housing, renewable energy and other investments.
markets: Israeli commercial property and North American multifamily housing, with other investment holdings.
rationale: B2B holding company with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality has limited value for a landlord and investor.

name: Ashtrom Properties
desc: Owns offices, shopping centres, hotels and residential projects in Israel and the United States, earning rental and development income.
markets: Property holdings in Israel and the US; part of Ashtrom group, a Tel Aviv-based developer.
rationale: Property developer with US and Israeli assets and hotel holdings; F1 hospitality could support sales, but brand is largely domestic.

name: RAIT Financial Trust
desc: Real estate investment trust; the entity behind this Crunchbase listing could not be confirmed.
markets: US real estate; company identity and current status not confirmed.
rationale: Identity unclear and no evident consumer brand or international activity; no F1 rationale.

name: Ares Commercial Real Estate
desc: Externally managed REIT that originates senior floating-rate loans on US commercial properties and earns net interest income and fees.
industry: commercial mortgage real estate investment trust
markets: Borrowers owning US commercial properties; managed by Ares Management's real estate group.
rationale: Financial vehicle with no consumer brand, though manager Ares Management has wider reach; weak F1 fit for the REIT itself.

name: REIT1
desc: Israeli real estate investment company that owns income-producing commercial properties, mainly offices and logistics sites, earning rent from tenants.
markets: Corporate tenants in Israel; no verified international operations.
rationale: Asset owner with no consumer brand and Israel-only portfolio; little commercial rationale for F1.

name: Y.H. Dimri
desc: Israeli construction and real estate company building residential and commercial projects, developing land and holding income-producing property.
markets: Home buyers, tenants and public bodies in Israel; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Regional Israeli developer with low brand awareness outside the country; no clear F1 rationale.

name: Al Hamra Real Estate Development
hq: Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates
desc: Develops Al Hamra Village in Ras Al Khaimah, a waterfront community with homes, golf, marina, mall and hotel.
markets: Residents, buyers and tourists in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE; international property buyers likely but not verified.
rationale: Gulf resort-property brand with international buyer appeal; F1 hospitality could suit property sales, but scale is modest.

name: 8990 Holdings
desc: Develops affordable condominium and housing projects in the Philippines, including Urban Deca Homes and Deca Homes, for middle-income buyers.
markets: Middle-income home buyers in the Philippines; no verified overseas operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Philippine consumer property brand with local audience; limited international ambitions make F1 a poor fit.

name: Invitation Homes
desc: Owns and leases about 85,000 single-family rental homes in US markets such as Atlanta, Phoenix, South Florida and Southern California.
industry: single-family rental real estate investment trust
markets: Residents renting homes in US markets in the Sun Belt and West; no international operations.
rationale: US-only landlord with resident-facing brand; little international or hospitality benefit from F1.
changed: Merged with Starwood Waypoint Homes in 2017

name: Somnigroup International
desc: Makes and sells Tempur-Pedic, Sealy and Stearns & Foster mattresses and operates Mattress Firm retail stores across the United States.
markets: Strong in North America with Tempur products sold in international markets; Mattress Firm stores in the US.
rationale: Consumer sleep brands with sports and celebrity marketing history; F1 offers premium audience and international reach for Tempur-Pedic, though no obvious tech tie-in.
changed: Tempur Sealy International renamed Somnigroup in 2025 after acquiring Mattress Firm

name: Urban Company
desc: Runs an app-based marketplace for at-home services such as cleaning, beauty, repairs and appliance servicing, and sells Native water purifiers.
markets: Operates across Indian cities and in the UAE; expansion into other overseas markets not verified here.
rationale: Large Indian consumer app brand with Gulf presence; F1 could aid brand building and trust among affluent urban users, though domestic focus limits global value.
changed: Formerly UrbanClap; listed in India in 2025

name: HomeServe USA
desc: Sells home emergency repair plans covering plumbing, sewer, electrical and HVAC to US homeowners, often co-branded with utilities and municipalities.
markets: US homeowners via utility and municipal partnerships; parent HomeServe operates in several other countries.
rationale: Direct-mail consumer service brand with utility partnerships; F1 offers little beyond general awareness for a US-only business.
changed: Parent HomeServe plc acquired by Brookfield in 2025

name: HNI Corporation
desc: Makes workplace furniture under HON, Allsteel and Kimball brands and residential building products such as Heatilator and Quadra-Fire fireplaces.
markets: Sells through dealers, retailers and builders in North America.
rationale: B2B furniture and hearth maker with North American focus; F1 hospitality could suit dealer and corporate relationship building, but brand fit is modest.

name: Asian Paints
desc: Makes decorative and industrial paints, waterproofing, wood finishes and home decor products sold through dealers, mainly in India.
markets: India's largest paint maker with operations in about 15 countries across Asia, Africa and the Middle East.
rationale: Strongest Indian paint brand with long cricket and TV advertising and overseas markets; F1 could widen reach, though rival paint brands already sponsor.

name: JSW Paints
desc: Sells interior and exterior decorative paints and related products through dealers across India for the JSW Group.
markets: Dealer network across India; acquired AkzoNobel India (Dulux) stake in 2025; no verified operations elsewhere.
rationale: Challenger paint brand from a group already active in sports sponsorship; F1 could build awareness, but customers are Indian only.
changed: Acquired controlling stake in AkzoNobel India (Dulux) in 2025

name: JELD-WEN
desc: Manufactures interior and exterior doors and windows sold to builders, distributors and home improvement retailers.
markets: Operations in North America, Europe and Australasia; customers are builders, distributors and home improvement stores.
rationale: B2B building products maker with consumer visibility through retail channels; F1 hospitality could support customer relationships, but brand is not motorsport-linked.

name: Sovereign Network Group
desc: Not-for-profit social housing provider owning more than 100,000 homes in southern England, formed by merging Sovereign and Network Homes.
markets: Tenants and shared owners in southern England; no international operations.
rationale: Not-for-profit housing association serving tenants; sponsoring F1 would be hard to justify and unlikely.
changed: Formed in 2023 by merger of Sovereign Housing Association and Network Homes

name: Pepperfry
desc: Sells furniture and home decor online and through studios and stores across Indian cities, from third-party sellers and own brands.
markets: Indian consumers shopping online and in studios; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Recognised Indian home furnishing brand with domestic customers only; limited reason to sponsor F1.

name: Floor & Decor
desc: Operates warehouse-style stores selling tile, wood, laminate, stone and decorative flooring accessories to homeowners and contractors across the United States.
markets: More than 250 stores in about 30 US states plus online sales; no international operations.
rationale: US-only specialty retailer with notable sports and TV advertising; F1 offers contractor hospitality but little international value.

name: Dweva
desc: Dallas-based home decor and furniture business; its products, scale and ownership are not confirmed.
markets: Furniture and decor sold to consumers; scope not verified.
rationale: Little known company with unclear scale and brand; no evident F1 rationale.

name: Porch Group
desc: Provides software and home insurance for homeowners through Homeowners of America and Porch Insurance, linking them with home services.
markets: Homeowners, home inspectors and moving companies in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: US-focused insurer and software firm with moderate homeowner recognition; F1 would add limited value beyond brand awareness.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq through a SPAC merger in 2020

name: Livspace
desc: Provides home interior design and renovation services, including modular kitchens and wardrobes, through its website, experience centres and designers.
markets: Operates in India, Singapore, Malaysia and the Middle East; customers are homeowners and designers.
rationale: Consumer design brand present in India, South-East Asia and the Gulf; F1 could suit affluent urban audiences, but marketing budget scale is modest.

name: Spectrum Brands
desc: Sells consumer products including Remington shavers, George Foreman grills, Tetra pet care and Cutter home and garden products.
markets: Sells through retailers such as Walmart, Amazon and Home Depot in the US and other markets worldwide.
rationale: Consumer brands with large retail reach could use F1 for activation, but portfolio is fragmented and Black+Decker is licensed.

name: Wakefit
desc: Sells mattresses, beds, sofas, furniture and home furnishings directly to Indian consumers online and through company-owned experience stores.
markets: Indian consumers online and via company-owned stores; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Heavily advertised Indian consumer brand; F1 could raise awareness among urban buyers, but audience is domestic.
changed: Listed on Indian exchanges in 2025

name: Sagist Group
desc: Designs and makes classic and contemporary luxury furniture for residential and hotel projects in Turkey and export markets.
markets: Turkey plus exports reportedly to the Middle East and Europe; details unconfirmed.
rationale: Niche luxury furniture maker with project-based customers; F1 hospitality could suit hotel and developer clients, but little is known about scale.

name: RentoMojo
desc: Rents furniture, appliances, electronics and fitness equipment on monthly plans to customers in Indian cities, with options to buy later.
markets: Young professionals and movers in Indian cities including Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi NCR.
rationale: Digitally marketed Indian consumer brand; domestic young-renter audience makes F1 a weak fit.

name: Lifetime Brands
desc: Designs and markets kitchenware, tableware and home products under brands including Farberware, Mikasa, Pfaltzgraff, Sabatier and licensed KitchenAid.
markets: Sells to department stores, mass retailers and online in the US, UK and other markets.
rationale: Household brands with retail reach in several markets; F1 could aid consumer and retailer activation, though parent is little known.

name: Neighborhood Intelligence
desc: Utah-based company classified under e-commerce and furniture; its products, customers and ownership could not be confirmed.
markets: Business activities not verified; located in Utah; no international operations known.
rationale: Company not recognised and activities unverified; there is no evident rationale for an F1 partnership.

name: ToughBuilt Industries
desc: Made tool belts, workbenches, knee pads, hand tools and storage for tradespeople, sold through Home Depot, Lowe's and Amazon.
markets: Retail customers in the United States and Canada; the company has ceased as a going concern.
rationale: Reportedly in bankruptcy and no longer operating; no basis for an F1 partnership.
changed: Filed for bankruptcy in 2024

name: Amplius
desc: Housing association based in Milton Keynes that owns and manages social and affordable homes in England.
markets: Tenants in England; scale and ownership not confirmed here.
rationale: Social housing provider with local brand only; sponsoring Formula 1 is unlikely to suit its purpose.

name: Maisons du Monde
desc: Sells furniture, lighting, textiles and decor under its own design brand through about 350 stores and online, mainly to consumers.
markets: Stores and online sales in France and other European countries; smaller professional business.
rationale: Design-led European home brand with international store network; F1 could aid awareness in Europe, though audience is consumer retail focused.

name: The Range
desc: Operates large UK superstores selling homeware, furniture, DIY, crafts, toys, pet supplies and seasonal goods, plus online.
markets: About 200 out-of-town stores serving UK households; no verified international operations.
rationale: Large UK retailer with family ownership and mass-market audience; Silverstone fans overlap, but little international benefit from F1.

name: Furlenco
desc: Rents beds, sofas, wardrobes, appliances and electronics to urban Indian households on monthly plans with delivery and maintenance included.
markets: Young professionals and families in about a dozen Indian cities; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Digitally advertised Indian rental brand with domestic customers; F1 offers weak value.

name: EigenCOMM
desc: Designs low-power wireless communication chips and modules for the Internet of Things, including NB-IoT and Cat.1 devices.
markets: Customers are IoT device and module makers, mainly in China; extent of overseas sales not confirmed.
rationale: B2B component supplier with no consumer brand; F1 technology showcase possible but limited strategic fit.

name: M/I Homes
desc: Designs, builds and sells single-family houses and townhomes, with mortgage and title services, in more than a dozen US markets.
markets: Home buyers in US markets including Ohio, Indiana, Florida, Texas, the Carolinas and the mid-Atlantic.
rationale: US regional homebuilder with local brand awareness; F1 offers little relevance to its buyers.

name: Ellos Group
desc: Sells fashion, home furnishings and interior products online and by catalogue under Ellos, Jotex and Homeroom brands in the Nordics.
markets: Consumers in Sweden, Norway and Finland, with long-established Nordic brands.
rationale: Well-known Nordic retail brand, but regional consumer focus and unclear marketing budget make F1 a weak fit.

name: Easyhome
desc: Operates large furniture and home improvement shopping centres across China, earning rent and management fees from merchants, plus online retail.
markets: National store network in China; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Well-known Chinese home furnishing brand with national reach; Chinese Grand Prix link possible, but domestic business limits value.

name: Stanza Living
desc: Runs branded co-living and student housing with furnished rooms, meals and services for students and young professionals in Indian cities.
markets: Students and young professionals in Indian cities including Delhi, Bengaluru, Pune and Hyderabad, paying monthly rent.
rationale: Growing consumer brand among Indian students and parents; F1 offers limited fit for a domestic accommodation business.

name: Saudi Company for Hardware (SACO)
desc: Operates large home improvement stores and e-commerce selling hardware, tools, building materials, decor, kitchenware and furniture, including private-label lines.
markets: Households, contractors and businesses across Saudi Arabia through large stores and online; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Familiar national retail brand in Saudi Arabia, host of an F1 Grand Prix; hospitality could reward contractors and customers, but footprint is domestic.

name: DFS Furniture
desc: Sells made-to-order sofas through about 100 UK showrooms and online, and owns Sofology, Sofa Workshop and Dwell.
markets: Mass-market and mid-market UK households through showrooms and online; no verified international operations.
rationale: Heavy TV advertiser with UK-only customers; British Grand Prix audience matches, but F1 brings little international value.

name: Grupo Lamosa
desc: Makes ceramic floor and wall tiles, bathroom fixtures, adhesives and cement-based products under Lamosa, Interceramic, Vitromex and Nexcer brands.
industry: ceramic tile and building products maker
markets: Builders, distributors and consumers in Mexico, the US and Latin America.
rationale: Mexican building products group with consumer tile brands in the Americas; F1 could support brand visibility around the Mexico City Grand Prix.
changed: Acquired Interceramic in 2018

name: The Richman Group
desc: Develops, owns and invests in affordable and workforce apartment communities across the US using low-income housing tax credits.
markets: Renters and housing fund investors across the United States; no international operations.
rationale: B2B housing developer with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship does not suit its mission or audience.

name: NORNORM
desc: Offers subscription-based circular furniture for homes and offices, with 3D technology to configure products, to business and household customers.
markets: Business and household customers in Denmark paying monthly; expansion plans not verified.
rationale: Small design-led startup with modest awareness; F1 sponsorship scale does not fit.

name: HomeLane
desc: Designs and installs modular kitchens, wardrobes and full-home interiors through experience centres across Indian cities and an online design service.
markets: Indian homeowners in urban centres; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Digitally advertised Indian brand with urban home buyers; domestic audience makes F1 a stretch.

name: Akzo Nobel India
desc: Sells decorative paints, mainly under the Dulux brand, plus industrial, powder and protective coatings through dealers across India.
markets: Dealer network across India; majority-owned by AkzoNobel, which agreed in 2025 to sell its stake to JSW Paints.
rationale: Strong Indian consumer paint brand, but a domestic subsidiary changing owner; AkzoNobel's global Sikkens F1 deal sits at group level.
changed: JSW Paints agreed in 2025 to acquire AkzoNobel's majority stake; completion not confirmed here
f1: Parent AkzoNobel owns Sikkens, a Formula 1 partner (stake in India being sold to JSW Paints)

name: XMax
desc: Company in Commerce, California classed under furniture and home decor; its products, customers and scale could not be confirmed.
markets: Business activities not verified; located in California; international operations not known.
rationale: Business unconfirmed and no evident brand scale; there is no clear rationale for an F1 partnership.

name: Zeus Living
desc: Leased and furnished apartments for business travellers and relocating employees on flexible terms through a booking platform, and later closed.
markets: Relocation managers and business travellers in US cities; the business later ceased operations.
rationale: Ceased operations and was a niche B2B brand; no F1 partnership possible.
changed: Ceased operations

name: Kokuyo
desc: Makes Campus notebooks, staplers, binders and files, plus office furniture and workplace design for corporate customers.
markets: Sells across Asia with operations in China, Southeast Asia and Australia; office furniture sold to corporations.
rationale: Well-known Japanese consumer and office brand with Asia-Pacific presence; F1 could support Asian corporate hospitality, but no obvious tech or motorsport tie-in.

name: Qumei Home Furnishings
desc: Makes and sells furniture including sofas, beds, wardrobes and whole-home customised furniture through franchised and self-operated stores and online.
markets: Chinese consumers via franchised and company stores, online channels and developer projects; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Known Chinese furniture name with recent losses; domestic focus and financial strain make F1 unlikely.

name: Stanley Lifestyles
desc: Makes and sells high-end sofas, recliners, dining sets and leather furniture through dozens of branded stores across India.
markets: Wealthy urban households, designers, hotels and corporate clients in India; also stocks international brands.
rationale: Luxury positioning among affluent Indians suits F1 hospitality, but business is India-only and small.
changed: Listed on Indian exchanges in 2024

name: Westwing
desc: Sells home furnishings, decor and furniture online through a member shopping club and own-label Westwing Collection products.
markets: Consumers in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Poland and other European markets.
rationale: Design-led European e-commerce brand; F1 could build awareness with affluent online shoppers, but audience is regional.

name: Home24
desc: Sold furniture, lighting and decor online to consumers in Germany, Austria, Switzerland and France.
markets: Online shoppers in Germany, Austria, Switzerland and France; now part of XXXLutz.
rationale: Now a unit of a larger Austrian furniture group; independent sponsorship is unlikely.
changed: Acquired by XXXLutz in 2022

name: One Kings Lane
desc: Sold designer furniture, rugs, lighting and accessories online through flash sales and a marketplace in the United States.
markets: US online home shoppers; current ownership and trading status not confirmed.
rationale: Past venture-backed US online brand with unclear current status; weak F1 fit.
changed: Acquired by Bed Bath & Beyond in 2016

name: eve Sleep
desc: Sold boxed mattresses, bed frames, pillows and bedding to UK consumers online and in showrooms, until its brand was sold.
markets: UK consumers with limited European presence; no longer trades independently.
rationale: No longer trades as an independent company, so no F1 partnership is realistic.
changed: Brand and assets sold to Dreams in 2022 after administration; delisted

name: Vilniaus Baldai
desc: Manufactures wooden and upholstered furniture, selling mainly to retailers and furniture chains across Europe.
markets: Retailers and furniture chains in Europe through exports; production in Vilnius.
rationale: B2B contract manufacturer with little consumer brand; F1 sponsorship is a poor fit.

name: Knoll
desc: Designs and makes office and residential furniture and textiles, including the Barcelona chair and Womb chair, sold through dealers.
markets: Corporate, education and healthcare clients via dealers and showrooms in North America and other markets.
rationale: Design brand now inside MillerKnoll; F1 design and luxury hospitality could suit architects, but decisions sit with the parent.
changed: Acquired by Herman Miller in 2021, forming MillerKnoll

name: Kujiale (Manycore Tech)
desc: Provides cloud 3D design software, Kujiale and Coohom, for interior designers, home builders and furniture brands.
markets: Serves designers, furniture brands and developers in China; Coohom is its product for overseas users.
rationale: B2B design software with technology showcase potential; F1 offers some tech tie-in, but limited consumer brand.

name: To8to
desc: Runs an online home renovation platform connecting homeowners with design and renovation companies, plus construction supervision and building-material sales.
markets: Homeowners and renovation contractors across China's major cities; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Heavily advertised Chinese consumer platform, but domestic audience limits value from an F1 deal.

name: Hardwoods Distribution
desc: Distributes hardwood and softwood lumber, panels, mouldings, doors and flooring to woodworkers, cabinet makers, builders and manufacturers.
markets: Professional customers through distribution centres in Canada and the United States.
rationale: B2B distributor with low consumer awareness; there is little rationale for an F1 partnership.

name: Angi
desc: Operates an online marketplace where homeowners find and book home service professionals, who pay for leads, advertising and memberships.
markets: Homeowners and service professionals mainly in the United States and Canada, with some European operations.
rationale: Well-known US consumer marketplace; F1 could build awareness, but audience is mostly North American.
changed: Separated from IAC in 2025

name: Supreme Industries
desc: Makes plastic piping systems, moulded furniture, material-handling crates and industrial components sold through dealers to construction and agricultural customers.
markets: Dealers and customers across India with more than 20 plants; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Indian B2B plastics maker recognised by builders; limited marketing culture and domestic reach make F1 weak.

name: Uniply Industries
desc: Indian listed manufacturer of wood-based panel and furniture-related products; its range and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Indian market; product range and customers not verified.
rationale: Small domestic manufacturer with unclear brand scale; there is no clear rationale for an F1 partnership.

name: Carpetright
desc: Sold carpets, beds and wood flooring through several hundred UK stores and online, with fitting services.
markets: UK household consumers through high-street and out-of-town stores; no international operations.
rationale: Entered administration and was bought by Tapi, so independent sponsorship is unrealistic.
changed: Entered administration in 2024 and bought by Tapi

name: Kering
desc: Owns luxury fashion and jewellery houses including Gucci, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta, Balenciaga and Alexander McQueen, plus Kering Eyewear.
markets: Affluent consumers worldwide via own boutiques, e-commerce and wholesale; run by the Pinault family's holding.
rationale: Global luxury group whose rival LVMH sponsors F1; F1's wealthy audience and paddock hospitality suit brand building.

name: Swarovski
desc: Makes precision-cut crystal, selling jewellery, accessories and home decor through own boutiques and e-commerce, and supplying crystal to fashion brands.
markets: Sells worldwide through boutiques, e-commerce and wholesale; operations centre in Wattens, Austria.
rationale: Global consumer brand with fashion and entertainment tie-ins; F1 offers glamour audience and B2B hospitality.

name: PC Jeweller
desc: Sells gold, diamond and silver jewellery through about 70 showrooms and online, mainly in northern India.
markets: Jewellery customers in India, strongest in the north; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Regional Indian jewellery brand with modest advertising and past debt restructuring; weak F1 fit.

name: BlueStone
desc: Sells certified gold and diamond jewellery through its website and a growing chain of about 275 stores in India.
markets: Indian consumers online and in stores; no verified overseas operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Digitally advertised jewellery brand with domestic customers; F1 could raise awareness among affluent Indians, but international value is small.
changed: Listed on Indian exchanges in 2025

name: Indriya Jewellery
desc: Jewellery and luxury goods company listed in Crunchbase; its location, products, scale and ownership could not be confirmed.
markets: Location, markets and customers not confirmed; no international activity or plans known.
rationale: Company identity and scale are unclear; no evidence supports an F1 partnership.

name: Kalyan Jewellers
desc: Sells gold, diamond and gemstone jewellery under the Kalyan and Candere brands through showrooms in India and the Middle East.
markets: Consumers in India, especially for weddings and festivals, plus showrooms in the Middle East.
rationale: Very strong Indian consumer brand with Gulf presence and heavy advertising; F1 could extend reach among Indian and Gulf audiences.
changed: Listed in India in 2021

name: Birks Group
desc: Designs and retails luxury jewellery, watches and gifts under Maison Birks and Mayors, with about 30 Canadian boutiques.
markets: Boutiques in Canada and Mayors stores in Florida and Georgia; retails third-party watch brands in Canada.
rationale: Upscale Canadian jeweller with a watch-retail business; F1 hospitality suits high-end clients, but footprint is small and North American.

name: Rosy Blue
desc: Cuts, polishes and supplies diamonds and manufactures jewellery for retailers and brands worldwide.
markets: B2B supplier with operations in Belgium, India, Hong Kong and the US selling to retailers and brands.
rationale: B2B diamond supplier with little consumer profile; F1 hospitality could suit trade clients, but marketing need is low.

name: Sky Gold
desc: Designs and manufactures plain and studded gold jewellery, selling mainly to jewellers and retail chains in India.
markets: Jewellers, retailers and brands across India; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: B2B gold manufacturer with little consumer brand; there is a weak rationale for F1.

name: Brilliant Earth
desc: Sells engagement rings, wedding bands and fine jewellery online and through US showrooms, with ethically sourced and lab-grown diamonds.
markets: Consumers in the US, with showrooms also in Canada and the UK; mainly engaged couples.
rationale: Known direct-to-consumer bridal brand; F1's affluent audience overlaps, but marketing is largely digital and North American.

name: Galderma
desc: Makes injectable aesthetics such as Restylane, Dysport and Sculptra, plus dermatological skincare including Cetaphil and Differin and prescription treatments.
markets: Sells to dermatologists, healthcare professionals and consumers via pharmacies in about 90 countries.
rationale: Global skincare and aesthetics brand with consumer-facing Cetaphil; F1's global audience could support brand building, but dermatology marketing is professional-led.
changed: Listed on SIX Swiss Exchange in 2024

name: L'Oréal
desc: Owns beauty brands including L'Oréal Paris, Lancôme, Maybelline, Garnier, Kiehl's, YSL Beauté, CeraVe and La Roche-Posay.
markets: Sells cosmetics, hair and skincare to consumers worldwide; the Bettencourt Meyers family is the largest shareholder.
rationale: World's largest beauty group with global ambassadors and sponsorships; F1 offers worldwide audience and a brand it already owns in the paddock.

name: THG
desc: Runs online beauty and nutrition retail brands such as LookFantastic, Cult Beauty and Myprotein, and the THG Ingenuity e-commerce platform.
markets: Consumers in more than 160 countries plus brand partners using its e-commerce platform.
rationale: Sports-linked consumer brands with global online reach; F1 offers athlete-style marketing and a technology showcase for THG Ingenuity.
changed: Formerly The Hut Group; listed in London in 2020

name: Coty
desc: Makes fragrance, cosmetics and skincare brands such as CoverGirl, Rimmel, Sally Hansen and Max Factor and holds fashion fragrance licences.
markets: Sells to consumers through department stores, mass retailers and online worldwide.
rationale: Global fragrance licensee of fashion brands including F1 partner brands; F1 could support licence activation and global retail reach.
f1: Fragrance licensee for BOSS and HUGO, Formula 1 partner brands (licence relationship only)

name: Estée Lauder Companies
desc: Sells prestige skincare, makeup and fragrance under Estée Lauder, Clinique, MAC, La Mer, Tom Ford Beauty and Jo Malone London.
markets: Sells in about 150 countries through department stores, travel retail and online; controlled by the Lauder family.
rationale: Prestige beauty brands with affluent global customers; F1 offers premium audience, hospitality and global travel-retail tie-ins.

name: dsm-firmenich
desc: Produces flavours, fragrances, nutritional ingredients, vitamins and health and beauty ingredients for food, perfume, personal care and pharma customers.
markets: B2B customers worldwide in food and drink, perfumery, personal care, pharma and animal feed; Dutch-Swiss group.
rationale: B2B ingredient supplier with low consumer visibility; F1 hospitality could suit key customer relationships, but marketing fit is weak.
changed: Formed in 2023 by merger of DSM and Firmenich

name: Procter & Gamble
desc: Makes household and personal care brands including Tide, Pampers, Gillette, Oral-B, Pantene, Always, Olay and Ariel, sold through retailers worldwide.
markets: Sells in about 180 countries through retailers; long-standing Olympic partner and large sports advertiser.
rationale: Global consumer giant already linked to F1 through Gillette; further brand activations across its portfolio are plausible.

name: Shein
desc: Sells inexpensive apparel, beauty, home goods and accessories to consumers through its app and website, using an on-demand supply chain.
markets: Consumers in more than 150 countries; headquartered in Singapore, founded in China.
rationale: Very high awareness among young shoppers and global reach suit F1 audience growth, though supply-chain scrutiny is a reputational consideration.

name: Valentino
desc: Luxury fashion house selling ready-to-wear, accessories, shoes, beauty and fragrance through boutiques, department stores and e-commerce worldwide.
markets: Sells worldwide through boutiques, department stores and online; owned by Qatar's Mayhoola, with Kering agreeing to take a 30% stake.
rationale: Globally recognised luxury brand with affluent customers; F1 hospitality could suit clients, though it has limited sports ties.
changed: Kering agreed in 2023 to take a 30% stake

name: SharkNinja
desc: Makes household appliances, including Shark vacuums and air purifiers and Ninja blenders, air fryers, coffee makers and grills.
markets: Sells through retail and online in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Heavily advertised consumer brands with global retail reach; already an F1 partner, so its activation scale is proven.
changed: Separated from JS Global and listed on NYSE in 2023
f1: SharkNinja is itself a Formula 1 partner (Nov 2026 roster)

name: Oddity Tech
desc: Builds digital-first beauty and wellness brands, including Il Makiage and SpoiledChild, sold directly to consumers online.
markets: Sells online mainly to women, with operations in New York and Tel Aviv.
rationale: Data-driven direct-to-consumer beauty marketer with heavy social media advertising; F1 could add premium reach, though its model is digital.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq in 2023

name: Cheplapharm
desc: Acquires and markets established branded prescription medicines from large pharma companies, such as Zovirax, Lariam and Xenical.
markets: Sells to pharmacies, hospitals and health systems in more than 100 countries.
rationale: B2B pharma with no consumer brand and heavy debt; weak F1 fit.

name: Market Kurly
desc: Runs a South Korean online grocery and beauty platform known for overnight Morning Delivery of fresh food and household goods.
markets: Urban households in South Korea; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Strong Korean e-commerce brand with domestic customers only, so Formula 1 sponsorship is a weak fit.

name: Debenhams Group
desc: Operates online fashion and beauty brands including Debenhams, Karen Millen, Coast, Warehouse and boohoo, selling in the UK and abroad.
markets: Online shoppers in the UK and other countries; successor to the former boohoo group.
rationale: Widely known British retail brand with young online audience; F1 could aid awareness, but financial pressure may limit spending.
changed: Renamed Debenhams Group from boohoo Group in 2025

name: Hypera Pharma
desc: Makes over-the-counter, prescription and generic medicines plus consumer health and personal care products sold through Brazilian pharmacies and distributors.
markets: Pharmacies, hospitals and consumers in Brazil; limited reach elsewhere.
rationale: Brazil's largest drug maker with strong consumer health brands; Brazilian Grand Prix audience fits, but business is domestic.

name: Nykaa (FSN E-Commerce Ventures)
desc: Runs the Nykaa beauty, personal care and fashion app, website and physical stores, plus own brands such as Kay Beauty.
markets: Millions of consumers in India online and in stores; overseas activity is minor.
rationale: Strong Indian consumer brand with young female customers and heavy sports and celebrity marketing; F1 could widen reach, though audience is Indian.
changed: Listed in India in 2021

name: Bolt Threads
desc: Develops bio-based materials, including b-silk protein for beauty and personal care products and Mylo mycelium leather, for brand customers.
markets: B2B ingredient supplier working with cosmetics and fashion brands; scale and overseas sales not confirmed.
rationale: B2B materials startup with low consumer awareness; F1 technology showcase possible, but budget and brand fit are weak.
changed: Listed publicly through a SPAC merger in 2024

name: e.l.f. Beauty
desc: Sells affordable cosmetics and skincare under e.l.f. Cosmetics, e.l.f. SKIN, Naturium, Keys Soulcare and rhode through mass retailers and online.
markets: Gen Z and millennial consumers, mainly in the United States, via Target, Walmart and Ulta, with some international sales.
rationale: Social-media-led brand with young audience and growing international sales; F1's growing female and younger fan base suits its marketing.
changed: Acquired rhode in 2025

name: Wella Company
desc: Makes hair colour, care, styling and nail products under Wella Professionals, Clairol, OPI, Nioxin and ghd for salons and consumers.
industry: hair and nail beauty products maker
markets: Sells to salons, retailers and consumers in over 100 countries, with major operations in Germany and Switzerland.
rationale: Global professional and consumer beauty brands; F1 hospitality and fan reach could support salon channel and consumer brands.
changed: Acquired by Coty in 2016; majority sold to KKR in 2020

name: Bath & Body Works
desc: Sells body care, fragrance mists, soaps, candles and home fragrance through about 1,900 US and Canadian stores, online and franchises.
markets: Mainly US and Canadian mall and street stores, plus online and franchised stores in other regions.
rationale: Strong US consumer retail brand with franchise expansion overseas; F1 could support international franchise growth, though audience is mostly North American.
changed: Spun out of L Brands in 2021

name: Tiendas 3B
desc: Mexican discount retail chain selling household cleaning, personal hygiene, food and beverage and other everyday products.
markets: Everyday shoppers in Mexico; store count and ownership not confirmed.
rationale: Mexican discount retailer with domestic customers; Mexico City Grand Prix exists, but F1 sponsorship scale is unlikely to suit it.

name: Goodai Global
desc: South Korean K-beauty distribution and marketing company; its product range, customers and ownership are not confirmed.
markets: Based in Seoul; overseas markets and customers not confirmed.
rationale: Distribution firm with little known brand; there is no evident rationale for an F1 partnership.

name: Growve
desc: Consumer brand aggregator in beauty and personal care that acquires and scales online brands; its specific brands are not confirmed.
markets: Online sales of acquired brands; markets and scale not confirmed.
rationale: Brand aggregator with unclear portfolio; F1 sponsorship does not obviously suit it.

name: Yatsen Holding
desc: Owns beauty brands Perfect Diary, Little Ondine, Abby's Choice, Galenic and DR.WU, selling cosmetics and skincare mainly online.
markets: Consumers mainly in China through Tmall, Douyin and own stores; some brands sold outside China.
rationale: Celebrity-led Chinese beauty brand group with shrinking sales; F1 could add profile, but business is largely domestic.
changed: Listed on the NYSE in 2020
